findings.title: A smuggled own __proto__ key passed the ledger schema (backfilled, campaign C-1)
findings.symptom: A ledger file with an own "__proto__" top-level key was read and carried instead of refused.
findings.direct_cause: readLedger accepted unknown top-level keys (open schema).
why: Unknown keys were tolerated because the schema was open.
Caller-controlled strings (JSON keys) were handled like trusted property names.
No test fed prototype-named strings through any parser or public API.
findings.root_cause: Caller-controlled strings cross into object-property space with no boundary rule and no hostile-name test.
findings.instance_fix: 1b54c3e closed schema (LEDGER_TOP_KEYS)
findings.guard: test/ledger.test.mjs::campaign C-1: sakk-ledger.v1 is a CLOSED schema
findings.sweep: Ledger top level only at the time; widened to every public entry point by F-13.

findings.title: A fake-executor run's pass rate was readable as a real-model pass rate (backfilled, harness migration)
findings.symptom: An all-green FAKE run produced a number in the real-model pass-rate field.
findings.direct_cause: aggregateMetrics computed real_model_case_pass_rate regardless of executor mode.
why: The metric was derived from verdicts alone.
Executor mode (how strong the evidence is) was not an input to the metric.
Report formats had no field separating harness proof from model evidence.
findings.root_cause: Evidence strength is not part of report types, so a weak run can emit a strong-looking claim.
findings.instance_fix: 5c307b1 real_model_case_pass_rate null in FAKE mode
findings.guard: eval/__tests__/gold-m1-closeout.test.mjs::FAKE mode: real_model_case_pass_rate must be null
findings.sweep: Metrics only at the time; recurred in pack reports (F-03) and docs (F-19).

findings.title: A FAKE run could report regulatory requirements as COVERED
findings.symptom: pack-report.json read COVERED for every requirement after a fake-executor run.
findings.direct_cause: packReport derived status from verdicts only.
why: Status was a function of verdicts alone.
Executor mode was not passed to packReport.
The report type had no evidence-strength state (F-02's class).
findings.root_cause: Evidence strength is not part of report types, so a weak run can emit a strong-looking claim.
findings.instance_fix: 24aeca0 FAKE ⇒ HARNESS_ONLY; report carries executor_mode, meaning, run id, commit, stop info
findings.guard: eval/__tests__/case-packs.test.mjs::FAKE mode → HARNESS_ONLY for every requirement, even when every case passed
findings.sweep: Every customer-facing report emitter checked: metrics (F-02), pack report (this), certificate, bundle verifier (MODE_MISMATCH). See class mechanism RC-10.

findings.title: Packs held control-plane-only cases a real run refuses
findings.symptom: A shipped pack could never produce real evidence: its cases are refused by the real-run gate.
findings.direct_cause: validatePack did not check case execution_mode.
why: Pack validation checked only that case ids exist.
Nobody ran a pack's case list through the real-run authorization gate.
The assumption 'every gold case is model-runnable' was never measured.
findings.root_cause: An assumption about which cases a real run accepts was relied on without a test that exercises the real gate.
findings.instance_fix: 24aeca0 control_plane_only cases rejected at load
findings.guard: eval/__tests__/case-packs.test.mjs::each shipped pack passes the real-run case-type gate
findings.sweep: All shipped packs pass the gate; no other component selects cases for real runs.

findings.title: Pack mappings claimed more regulatory coverage than their cases show
findings.symptom: Requirements were mapped to cases that test something adjacent, with no statement of what is missing.
findings.direct_cause: The pack format had no field for gaps.
why: The format let a mapping exist without stating its limits.
Writing the mapping was the author's judgement with no structural check.
Customer-facing compliance claims had no 'what this does not show' requirement.
findings.root_cause: Claims in customer-facing artifacts are not structurally paired with their limits.
findings.instance_fix: 24aeca0 mandatory gaps (per requirement) and not_covered (per pack); packs rewritten
findings.guard: eval/__tests__/case-packs.test.mjs::missing not_covered, or a requirement without gaps, is invalid
findings.sweep: Packs, README claims, bundle README checked; doc-claim drift recurred in F-19.

findings.title: gold-runner --pack=value silently ran every case
findings.symptom: The equals form was not recognised; with no selector the runner ran all cases.
findings.direct_cause: val() only parses the space form; an unparsed selector meant 'no selector' = all cases.
why: The argument parser ignored a form it did not understand.
Absence of a selector defaulted to the widest action.
No negative test for the equals form existed.
findings.root_cause: Missing or unparsed input defaults to the permissive outcome instead of a refusal.
findings.instance_fix: 24aeca0 USAGE_EQUALS_FORM, exit 2
findings.guard: eval/__tests__/case-packs.test.mjs::unknown --pack exits 2; --case with --pack exits 2; --pack=x exits 2 instead of running everything
findings.sweep: sakk CLI val() refuses a missing value (F3, earlier); equals form on sakk CLI not checked — F-21.

findings.title: The commit hook resolved sakk through npx, and the test rewrote the hook before running it
findings.symptom: The installed hook ran whatever `npx sakk` resolved to; the test replaced that line, so the shipped hook was never exercised.
findings.direct_cause: Hook body `npx sakk scan --staged`; test substituted a local path.
why: The hook trusted package resolution at commit time.
The test substituted the shipped artifact with a stand-in.
Nothing required tests to exercise artifacts exactly as shipped.
findings.root_cause: A test stand-in replaced the shipped artifact, hiding a trust-boundary dependency on package resolution.
findings.instance_fix: 9799390 absolute node + realpath hook, wx write
findings.guard: test/secret-scan.test.mjs::the installed hook runs this installation by absolute path; clean commits pass, secret commits are refused
findings.sweep: Other shipped scripts: MCP config in README uses npx by user choice (documented); no other generated executables.

findings.title: Staged scan misread names like 0:foo and missed type changes
findings.symptom: A file literally named 0:foo was read as stage 0 of foo; a symlink-to-file type change was not scanned.
findings.direct_cause: `git show :path` parses the path; --diff-filter lacked T.
why: Paths were passed through git's revision syntax.
Test file names were all plain.
No test used hostile file names or type changes.
findings.root_cause: Test data did not represent hostile or unusual input shapes at an interface that parses its input.
findings.instance_fix: 9799390 ls-files -s -z blob ids + cat-file; ACMRT
findings.guard: test/secret-scan.test.mjs::a file literally named "0:foo" is read as itself, not as stage 0 of "foo" (review S-2)
findings.sweep: Other git invocations: certificate engine uses rev-parse/status only (no path syntax).

findings.title: A scan that could not look anywhere reported clean
findings.symptom: A mistyped path, an unreadable file, or an explicit dist/ path produced exit 0 'no findings'.
findings.direct_cause: Missing roots and read errors were skipped silently.
why: Errors during the walk were swallowed.
'Nothing found' and 'nothing looked at' had the same exit code.
No negative test for missing or unreadable input.
findings.root_cause: Missing or unreadable input defaults to the permissive outcome instead of a refusal.
findings.instance_fix: 9799390 SCAN_PATH_MISSING / SCAN_UNREADABLE exit 2; skips counted
findings.guard: test/secret-scan.test.mjs::a mistyped path exits 2 SCAN_PATH_MISSING
findings.sweep: See pattern fail-open-absence: F-06, F-09, F-16.

findings.title: Secret-scan patterns could backtrack catastrophically
findings.symptom: Unbounded quantifiers allowed super-linear time on crafted lines.
findings.direct_cause: Regexes without length bounds.
why: Patterns were written for typical input.
No hostile-input timing test existed.
Performance on adversarial input was assumed, not measured.
findings.root_cause: Linear-time behaviour on attacker-shaped input was assumed and never measured.
findings.instance_fix: 9799390 bounded quantifiers, binary-search line index
findings.guard: test/secret-scan.test.mjs::200KB adversarial lines for every rule scan without catastrophic backtracking
findings.sweep: Other regexes on caller input: policy scope matcher has POLICY_TOO_COMPLEX budget (earlier F4); match.mjs is glob, not regex.

findings.title: The exemption token anywhere in a match exempted a real password
findings.symptom: A DSN whose USERNAME contained the fiction token exempted its real password.
findings.direct_cause: Exemption checked the whole match text.
why: The exemption used a substring test on the full match.
Which part of the match is the secret was not modelled.
Tests placed the token only in the secret position.
findings.root_cause: A context-dependent judgement (which field holds the secret) was made with a whole-string match.
findings.instance_fix: 9799390 exemption judged on the secret capture group only
findings.guard: test/secret-scan.test.mjs::a token in the USERNAME does not exempt a real password (review)
findings.sweep: All eight rules declare their secret group; rules without one use the full match by design.

findings.title: Scan output could be reversed or leak secrets through paths
findings.symptom: Unkeyed sha256 fingerprints are dictionary-reversible from public CI logs; secret-bearing file names were printed.
findings.direct_cause: fingerprint = sha256(secret); paths printed verbatim.
why: A plain hash was assumed irreversible.
Paths were not treated as output that can carry secrets.
No test asserted output never contains secret material.
findings.root_cause: Output channels were not treated as a trust boundary: every printed field must be checked for secret material.
findings.instance_fix: 9799390 HMAC with per-run key; redacted paths counted as findings
findings.guard: test/secret-scan.test.mjs::a secret in a FILE NAME is redacted in output and counted as a finding (review)
findings.sweep: Other printers of caller data: sakk status prints agent ids and reasons (operator-supplied, not secrets); alerts log callIds.

findings.title: Agent ids that are prototype names broke the kill switch
findings.symptom: Halting agent __proto__ reported success but was never written; constructor/toString read as halted.
findings.direct_cause: h.agents[agentId] plain indexing and assignment.
why: Caller-supplied ids were used as plain object keys.
The fuzz agent pool held only benign names.
F-01 fixed the instance (ledger top level) without a class rule for every entry point.
findings.root_cause: Caller-controlled strings cross into object-property space with no boundary rule and no hostile-name test.
findings.instance_fix: cdab3bd Object.hasOwn reads, defineProperty writes, AGENT_ID_INVALID
findings.guard: test/kill-switch.test.mjs::never read as halted before a halt; halt is written to disk; refuse; resume lifts
findings.sweep: Swept src/, bin/, eval/lib, eval/bin, scripts/ for computed member access on caller data: only ledger agents map (fixed). Class detector: test/hostile-names.test.mjs.

findings.title: The halt field was added to a closed schema without a version bump
findings.symptom: sakk-ledger.v1 gained an optional key, against the documented closed-schema rule.
findings.direct_cause: LEDGER_TOP_KEYS extended in place.
why: The rule 'new fields mean a version bump' was a code comment.
Nothing failed when the v1 key list changed.
Schema discipline depended on the author remembering the comment.
findings.root_cause: A mandatory step (version bump on schema change) was enforced only by a comment.
findings.instance_fix: cdab3bd sakk-ledger.v2 on first halt; v1 forbids halt
findings.guard: test/kill-switch.test.mjs::genesis is v1 with no halt key; the first halt makes it v2; resume keeps v2 with an emptied record
findings.sweep: Other closed formats: case-pack schema, bundle schema, policy schema — pinned by detector test/schema-pins.test.mjs.

findings.title: A test without a timeout hung the mutation drill
findings.symptom: Under MUT-G the lock-storm test's workers looped forever; the drill never reported.
findings.evidence: this session: drill run on b56100c
findings.direct_cause: Workers loop until they see LEDGER_HALTED; no deadline, no test timeout.
why: The test waited for a condition the mutant removes.
node --test had no global timeout.
Neither the drill nor CI jobs bound runtime, so a hang is silent rather than red.
findings.root_cause: The measuring tools (test runner, drill, CI) had no bound on runtime, so a hang never becomes a failure.
findings.instance_fix: cdab3bd bounded workers + test timeout
findings.guard: test/kill-switch.test.mjs::CLI halt succeeds while 6 processes hammer the ledger
findings.sweep: All tests that spawn children reviewed; class fix: --test-timeout on every test script and timeout-minutes on every CI job.

findings.title: Falsy JSON in a bundle skipped the metrics recompute
findings.symptom: A forger who replaced a result with null and regenerated the manifest got VERIFY PASS.
findings.direct_cause: json() returned falsy values unflagged; a short case list skipped the recompute.
why: Unparseable or empty data was treated as 'skip this check'.
A skipped check produced no problem entry.
No test fed falsy JSON.
findings.root_cause: Missing or unreadable input defaults to the permissive outcome instead of a refusal.
findings.instance_fix: a576f79 CASE_FILE_INVALID / METRICS_UNVERIFIABLE

findings.title: The bundle's verifier was the only check an auditor was told to run
findings.symptom: verify.mjs ships inside the bundle; a forged bundle can ship a verifier that prints PASS.
findings.direct_cause: Docs said: unpack and run node verify.mjs.
why: The verification procedure trusted code inside the artifact under test.
The out-of-band fingerprint was printed by that same code.
No step required checking the artifact before executing it.
findings.root_cause: Code inside an untrusted artifact was treated as trusted.
findings.instance_fix: a576f79 shasum fingerprint + shasum -c before node verify.mjs (README and AUDITOR_REPLAY §6)
findings.guard: test/evidence-bundle.test.mjs::the bundle README orders the independent checks BEFORE running verify.mjs
findings.sweep: Other artifacts executed by auditors: none (certificate is data).

findings.title: Bundles could carry symlinks and the shipped archive was never verified
findings.symptom: A symlink in the run dir was copied into the bundle; only the staging dir was verified, not the tgz.
findings.direct_cause: cpSync copies links; tar output not re-verified.
why: The builder trusted the run directory's file types.
Verification ran on a stand-in (staging dir) for the shipped artifact.
No test planted a link or inspected the archive.
findings.root_cause: Verification ran on a stand-in for the shipped artifact, and link-following crossed a trust boundary.
findings.instance_fix: a576f79 regular files only, archive unpacked fresh and re-verified, exclusive link
findings.guard: test/evidence-bundle.test.mjs::a symlink in the run directory → BUNDLE_SOURCE_INVALID, nothing written
findings.sweep: Secret scan skips links (F-07 branch); ledger writes use wx (F15 earlier).

findings.title: Bundle docs claimed checks the verifier did not perform
findings.symptom: README listed consistency checks (mode, metrics) that were partly absent in code.
findings.direct_cause: Doc text and verifier code written separately with no link.
why: Claims were prose with no pointer to the code that enforces them.
No test compared documented checks to implemented ones.
Third occurrence of evidence-strength overclaim (F-02, F-03).
findings.root_cause: Claims in customer-facing artifacts are not structurally tied to the checks that back them.
findings.instance_fix: a576f79 docs list exactly what is and is not checked; code adds MODE_MISMATCH, CASE_SET_MISMATCH, metric recompute

Every test used absolute temp paths.

Unknown flags were not refused.

Model identity lived only in metrics.json.
Nothing tied the claim to the evidence of which binary ran.

findings.title: A REAL batch that stopped early exited 0
findings.symptom: Unknown cost stopped the batch after a passing case; the run exited 0 with cases NOT_RUN.
findings.direct_cause: exit = every(entry PASS) over the entries that ran.
why: Success was computed over what ran, not over what was selected.
Cases that never ran were absent, and absence counted as success.
No negative test for a stopped batch.
findings.root_cause: Missing or unparsed input defaults to the permissive outcome instead of a refusal.

findings.sweep: Bundle verifier treats a stopped batch as INCOMPLETE (F-33).

findings.symptom: Odd-length FE FF aborted the scan; ENOTDIR/EACCES exited 1 with a stack; umask 177 produced an ignored hook; a hostile install path injected shell; an npx-cache install pointed at a deleted path.

why: Tests ran in one benign environment.
Environment-dependent behaviour (umask, paths, caches) was not varied.
No checklist of hostile environments existed.
findings.root_cause: Test environments did not represent the shells, umasks, paths and caches real installs see.

why: Schemes were added one by one.

findings.title: Staged scanning did not scale
findings.symptom: 3000 staged files took 25 s; a 270 MB blob failed with ENOBUFS and no file name.

findings.instance_fix: this commit: runs refuse with HARNESS_GIT_REQUIRED unless git's top is sakk's root; harnessDirty returns null (unknown) there
findings.guard: eval/__tests__/stranger-regressions.test.mjs::an execution mode refuses with HARNESS_GIT_REQUIRED instead of naming the parent commit

findings.title: Deleting one key skipped the REAL model check and hid a modified harness
findings.symptom: A REAL bundle with metrics.model_id deleted verified PASS even after every trace was relabelled to another model; a run from a modified harness carried harness_dirty only in pack-report.json, which nothing checked; an older genuine verifier shipped in a bundle passed forgeries later versions catch.
findings.evidence: Fable 5 review of plan item ④ (2026-10-16): blocker + 2 should-fix; plan item ① S5
findings.direct_cause: The verifier read model_id as 'if present'; metrics.json never recorded harness_dirty; packReport read COVERED for any REAL run; the auditor procedure trusted the shipped verifier.
why: Each check was written for the forged value, not for the missing one.
Optional-by-default reads (`'k' in x`, `?? null`) turned absence into agreement.
No test deleted keys; forgeries in the suite only changed values.
findings.root_cause: An assumption about the environment was never verified (pattern fail-open-absence, 12th instance).
findings.instance_fix: this commit: REAL requires model_id (verifier + builder); every run records harness_dirty; REAL on a modified/unknown tree is INCOMPLETE and reads HARNESS_MODIFIED; pack report and bundle.json are closed; the auditor runs the current verifier from a clone
findings.class_fix: test/bundle-absence.test.mjs::every silently deletable key is declared, and every declaration is still needed
findings.guard: test/evidence-bundle.test.mjs::a REAL run whose metrics name no model → METRICS_UNVERIFIABLE, even with traces relabelled
findings.sweep: Exhaustive key deletion over a real pack bundle (every document, every key): 46 keys still pass, each declared with its reason (descriptive case fields, scorer evidence, ledger fields sakk itself does not require). Drill MUT-U/MUT-V hold the checks.

findings.title: The lock-storm test decided pass/fail with a 20 s deadline
findings.symptom: Under load the halt CLI took longer than the workers' 20 s window, every worker exited 3 and the test failed; 96 instrumented storms showed halt latency p50 1.4 s, max 8.1 s, and 0 reservations booked after any halt.
findings.evidence: kill-switch.test.mjs full-file run during this round; scratch storm harness (96 storms, 24-way concurrency)
findings.direct_cause: Workers stopped at Date.now() + 20000 and treated that as failure; the F-62 sweep and detector only matched `Date.now() - t` comparisons.
why: The test proved 'the halt is seen' with a clock, not with order.
The mkdir lock is not fair, so halt latency grows with load.
The class sweep searched one textual shape of the class.
findings.root_cause: The measuring tool's own logic was never tested against the conditions it runs in.
findings.instance_fix: this commit: workers learn the halt returned through a signal file; a reservation granted after it exits 5 (the bug), and no entry may be created after halt.at; 120 s is a hang guard only
findings.class_fix: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::no test or check script asserts speed with a tight wall clock
findings.guard: test/kill-switch.test.mjs::CLI halt succeeds while 6 processes hammer the ledger
findings.sweep: Detector extended to deadline shapes (Date.now() + literal); fault-injection's +3600_000 is a fixture timestamp, soak's minutes-based deadline is a campaign length, not a pass/fail bound.

findings.title: Halting or resuming a stale ledger made it fresh
findings.symptom: halt({agentId:'bot'}) on a 365-day-old ledger restamped updatedAt, so an anonymous reserve that refused LEDGER_STALE before the halt succeeded after it.
findings.evidence: Fable 5 review of plan item ③ (2026-10-16), S1
findings.direct_cause: writeLedger stamps updatedAt on every write, including halt and resume.
why: updatedAt means 'books confirmed', but it was written as 'file touched'.
The halt path reads with infinite staleness on purpose, then wrote a fresh stamp.
No test combined a stale ledger with a stop.
findings.root_cause: A value's meaning was used outside its scope: a file-touched stamp stood in for books-confirmed.
findings.instance_fix: this commit: halt and resume keep updatedAt
findings.class_fix: test/kill-switch.test.mjs::each writeLedger call sits in a classified function, with the matching option
findings.guard: test/kill-switch.test.mjs::review S1: halting or resuming a STALE ledger never makes it fresh
findings.sweep: Other writes that confirm nothing about the books: none — settle/mark/clear are money operations and keep refreshing.

findings.title: Who lifted a halt lived only in the best-effort alert log
findings.symptom: With sakk-alerts.jsonl unwritable, resume({by:'mallory'}) succeeded and the name appeared nowhere; the spec called resume signed.
findings.evidence: Fable 5 review of plan item ③ (2026-10-16), S2
findings.direct_cause: resume() nulled the record and wrote the resumer only to emitAlert, which swallows errors.
why: Alerts are best-effort so a broken alert path never blocks a stop.
The same best-effort channel was used for evidence that must survive.
Nothing tested the record after a resume with the alert path broken.
findings.root_cause: Produced without verification.
findings.instance_fix: this commit: halt.lifts (append-only, closed entries) records by/at/scope/agentId/haltedBy/haltedAt in the ledger; deleting it refuses

findings.title: Two kill-switch guarantees were held only by a probabilistic fuzz
findings.symptom: A scoped resume that also cleared the global halt, a global resume that wiped agent halts, and reconciliation checked before the halt all passed npm test; the fuzz caught the first on some seeds only.
findings.evidence: Fable 5 review of plan item ③ (2026-10-16), S3+S4 (mutants M1, M2, M3)
findings.direct_cause: Spec rows claimed named tests, but the tests drove only CLI usage errors, not the library path.
why: Row tests were written for the CLI attack, not for the library guarantee.
The fuzz was counted as the guard although its seed is Date.now().
No mutation targeted resume scoping.
findings.root_cause: Produced without verification.
findings.instance_fix: this commit: deterministic tests for both resume directions and halt-over-reconciliation; drill MUT-W
findings.guard: test/kill-switch.test.mjs::a scoped resume leaves the global halt in force
findings.sweep: Adversary rows 17-20 added with named tests; each M1/M2/M3 mutant applied by hand dies.

findings.title: Kill-switch nits: raw control characters in status, blank names, docs that disagreed
findings.symptom: `sakk status` printed `--by $'\e[2J'` raw; halt records accepted by ' ' and agents['']; the README put 'exits 4' under the per-agent example; the spec said null was anonymous for halt/resume while row 15 refuses it.
findings.evidence: Fable 5 review of plan item ③ (2026-10-16), nits
findings.direct_cause: Operator input reached the terminal unescaped; validation checked non-empty, not non-blank; docs were edited row by row.
why: Names were treated as trusted because operators type them.
Escaping existed for file names only.
Doc rows were not cross-read after row 15 landed.
findings.root_cause: A trust boundary left undefended.
